Introduction
This document provides essential information on the components of the Packaging Material & Waste Key
Issue to enable users of ESG Ratings to understand how MSCI Sustainability & Climate’s (MSCI S&C’s)
outputs are determined. Packaging Material & Waste is a Key Issue in the Environmental Pillar of the
MSCI ESG Ratings model. Companies are evaluated on their production of or reliance upon packaging
materials, their potential exposure to waste management and packaging regulations, as well as their
efforts to reduce the environmental impact of packaging materials.
For additional details on the MSCI ESG Ratings Model, refer to the Data, ratings and scores section of
“ESG Ratings Methodology.”

Risks associated with this Key Issue
• Loss of access to markets due to reform of regulations governing packaging material and waste.
• Loss of revenue due to changing consumer preferences.
• Increased costs to reformulate packaging and comply with producer responsibility regulations.

The definitions of the data points in each component are given below:
Packaging Material & Waste Practices score
The Packaging Material & Waste Practices score evaluates the company’s ability to manage its exposure
to risks related to its production of or reliance upon packaging materials, as well as its efforts to reduce
the environmental impact of packaging materials. This score is a component of the Packaging Material &
Waste Management score (excluding controversies) and considers attributes of the company's policies
and initiatives. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.
• Disclosure of packaging material mix
Definition: How transparent the company is about the type of materials used in its packaging. Best
practice is full disclosure.
• Scope of consumer programs to reduce waste
Definition: The scope of the company’s consumer education programs on recycling (e.g., take-back
locations) or recycling instructions.
• Scope of recycling programs where not mandated by law

Definition: The extent of the company’s involvement in recycling or recovery of packaging materials in
locations or circumstances where packaging waste recycling is not mandated by law. Best practice is to
have an overarching packaging waste strategy.
• Strategy to reduce the environmental impact of packaging
Definition: The comprehensiveness of the company’s strategy to reduce the environmental impact of its
packaging, such as through waste elimination, packaging redesign, and engagement with suppliers or
customers. Best practice is to have specific initiatives that reduce the environmental impact of
packaging.
• Targets related to packaging content
Definition: Assesses the company's targets and their scope focused on recycled material content of
packaging. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating strong initiatives.
o Scope of targets to increase recycled material content of packaging
Definition: Indicates the scope of a company's target to incorporate postconsumer recycled
materials into its packaging.
o Targets to increase recycled or renewable material content of packaging
Definition: Indicates whether the company has specific targets for improving packaging
content, such as increasing recycled content, renewable content, or eliminating problematic
or hard-to-recycle plastic content.
• Targets related to packaging material circularity or waste elimination
Definition: Assesses the company's targets and their scope focused on packaging material circularity or
waste elimination. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating strong initiatives.
o Scope of targets for packaging material circularity or waste elimination
Definition: Indicates the scope of environmental targets related to material recovery or waste
elimination in packaging.
o Targets for packaging material circularity or waste elimination
• Definition: Indicates whether the company has specific targets related to
improving product recovery through packaging.

Packaging Material & Waste Performance score
The Packaging Material & Waste Performance score evaluates the company's performance on
packaging material & waste metrics (including achievements on packaging content and product
recovery). It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance.
• Scope of environmental improvements in packaging
Definition: Assesses the company's achievements on packaging content (e.g. light-weighted, recycled
content).
• Scope of product or packaging recovery
Definition: Assesses the company's achievements on product or packaging recovery.
Controversies
A controversy deduction ranging from 0 to 5 points is subtracted from the overall Management score
based on the severity, status, and the company’s role in the controversies facing the company on this
Key Issue. The following categories of controversies are used in the assessment:
• Packaging waste controversies.
For more details on how controversies are included in the MSCI ESG Ratings model, refer to the
Controversies cases section of “ESG Ratings Methodology.”

Business Segment Exposure scores

business segment as disclosed by the company to a corresponding business activity. MSCI S&C uses
the Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) system along with industry-specific adjustments to define
business activities. The score associated with a business activity is used to calculate a Business
Segment Exposure score.
Each business activity score is determined by a simple average of the Plastic Packaging Use and Waste
Intensity score and the Plastic Packaging Reliance score.

The Recycling Mandates score is based on a country’s recycling mandate policies’ stringency and the
extent to which the policies are applied within a country or market.
The Extended Producer Responsibility score is based on a country’s extended producer responsibility
regulations’ stringency and the extent to which the policies are applied within a country or market.
The Single-use Plastic Law score is based on a country’s single-use plastics regulations’ stringency and
the extent to which the policies are applied within a country or market.
The Plastic Waste Mismanagement score for each country is based on the quantity of plastic waste
generated per capita.
Data sources
The following sources are used to determine the Packaging Material & Waste Exposure score:
“Plastics Policy Inventory,” Duke University; United Nations Environment Programme, Legal Limits on
Single-Use Plastics and Microplastics: A Global Review of National Laws and Regulations; “What A
Waste Global Database,” World Bank; Cimpan, C., Bjelle, E.L., and Strømman, A.H., “Plastic packaging
flows in Europe: A hybrid input-output approach,” Journal of Industrial Ecology 25, no. 6: 1572-1587;
World Development Indicators, World Bank; Refinitiv; MSCI S&C; and company disclosures.
